The provost wants to review faculty workload balance across all departments. Start by fetching the faculty workload standards from http://localhost:30220/api/workload_standards.json which defines the maximum course load, student thresholds, grading time estimates, and overload criteria.

Then query the learning management system to determine each instructor's teaching load. For each instructor with a teaching role, count the number of distinct courses they teach, the total number of students across those courses, and the total number of assignments they are responsible for. Calculate the estimated total semester grading hours as total students multiplied by the grading hours per student from the standards. Then calculate the weekly grading hours by dividing the semester total by the number of semester weeks from the standards. An instructor is overloaded if they teach more than the maximum courses allowed OR if their weekly grading hours exceed the maximum weekly hours from the standards.

Review the workload policy document, faculty directory file, and the course-to-department mapping file (department_mapping.csv) in the workspace for context on department assignments and institutional policy.

Create an Excel file called Faculty_Workload.xlsx with two sheets. The first sheet named "Instructor Load" should contain columns for Instructor, Courses_Count, Total_Students, Total_Assignments, Est_Grading_Hours (total semester hours, rounded to 1 decimal), Weekly_Grading_Hours (rounded to 1 decimal), and Overloaded_YN. Sort alphabetically by instructor name. The second sheet named "Department Summary" should aggregate by department. Determine each course's department using department_mapping.csv: course names in the learning management system are formatted as "<Subject Area> (<Term> <Year>)" (for example, "Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2013)"); take the text before the first "(" as the subject area and match it case-insensitively and exactly (note the names contain "&") against the Course_Base_Name column in department_mapping.csv to get the Department. The sheet should have columns Department, Instructor_Count, Course_Count, and Total_Students. Instructor_Count is the number of distinct instructors who teach at least one course in that department (an instructor who teaches in multiple departments is counted in each). Course_Count is the number of course offerings in that department — count every offering, including any that have no instructor assigned (some offerings have no teacher). Total_Students is the sum of the student counts across all course offerings in that department, again including offerings with no instructor. Sort by Department alphabetically.

Write the workload data to a shared spreadsheet titled "Faculty Workload Analysis" with a sheet called "Instructor Load" containing the same instructor-level data.

Also create a presentation called Workload_Review.pptx summarizing the key findings. Include a title slide, a slide showing the total number of instructors and how many are overloaded, a slide with the department-level breakdown, and a recommendations slide suggesting rebalancing strategies for departments with overloaded faculty.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent completes the compact 22-course aggregation directly, freezes every result into one JSON handoff file, and uses exactly one parallel writer wave. Canvas is read-only. Resolve the runtime workspace dynamically. Do not dispatch any source or aggregation sub-agents.

Read workload_standards.json, the complete workload policy PDF, faculty_directory.csv and department_mapping.csv, and call canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true) once. Freeze the exact IDs/codes/full names for all 22 courses and the literal policy formulas/overload boundaries. Then issue native-parallel course calls: for every course, canvas_get_course_grades(page=1,per_page=100,type=["StudentEnrollment"]) and use pagination.total_count as Student_Count; canvas_get_course_grades(page=1,per_page=100,type=["TeacherEnrollment"]) retaining all teacher row.id/user_id; canvas_list_assignments(include_submissions=false); and canvas_list_course_users. Follow teacher pagination if advertised and read any roster full_output_path rather than a truncated preview.

The main agent joins each TeacherEnrollment user_id only to its course roster, counts distinct courses per instructor, and sums students and assignments over taught courses. Compute semester grading hours=Total_Students*grading_hours_per_student, weekly hours=semester hours/semester_weeks, and overload from either literal policy condition. For departments, use the exact case-insensitive mapping of the full base subject name before the first parenthesis; include every one of the 22 offerings, including no-teacher offerings.

Then freeze ALL results into a single handoff file workload_data.json in the runtime workspace with exactly these keys: "standards" (the literal workload standards object), "instructor_load" (the instructor rows with keys Instructor, Courses_Count, Total_Students, Total_Assignments, Est_Grading_Hours, Weekly_Grading_Hours, Overloaded_YN, already sorted alphabetically by Instructor), "department_summary" (department rows with keys Department, Instructor_Count, Course_Count, Total_Students, already sorted alphabetically by Department), "total_instructors", and "total_overloaded".

Wave 1 — start three Coder writers in parallel. Each writer must read ONLY workload_data.json for its data (no re-derivation from source systems) and must not touch any input file:

1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Sole writer of Faculty_Workload.xlsx. Build exactly two sheets from the JSON: "Instructor Load" with the header row Instructor, Courses_Count, Total_Students, Total_Assignments, Est_Grading_Hours, Weekly_Grading_Hours, Overloaded_YN and one row per instructor_load entry in the given order (hours as numeric values rounded to 1 decimal); "Department Summary" with the header row Department, Instructor_Count, Course_Count, Total_Students and one row per department_summary entry. Write to the runtime workspace path, then read back both sheets fully to verify headers, order and row counts.
2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Sole owner of the exact-title Google spreadsheet "Faculty Workload Analysis". Search/reuse-or-create at most once, keep exactly one sheet named "Instructor Load", write the frozen instructor_load table with the same header and values, then read it back and report the spreadsheet ID, title, sheet name and data-row count.
3. coder 2 (office-report-builder 1): Sole writer of Workload_Review.pptx. Build exactly four slides from the JSON: title slide; an overview slide stating total_instructors and total_overloaded; a department breakdown slide covering all departments; and an evidence-based recommendations slide for rebalancing overloaded departments. Verify slide titles and every numeric claim through presentation info and text extraction.

The main agent reconciles the two writer read-backs and the spreadsheet report against workload_data.json (22-course, instructor and department controls). No extra verification or repair wave is allowed.

You are a read-only Canvas LMS data analyst. You are completing ONE assigned part of a larger faculty-workload analysis for a university provost. You have no other context, and the data you return will be trusted verbatim, so be precise and complete.

Available Canvas MCP tools (use them; they are read-only for you):
- canvas_get_course_grades(course_id, type=["TeacherEnrollment"|"TaEnrollment"|"StudentEnrollment"], per_page, page) — returns enrollments plus a "pagination" block with total_count. Using type=["StudentEnrollment"] with per_page=1 gives you the total student count cheaply via pagination.total_count.
- canvas_list_assignments(course_id) — returns the list of assignment objects.
- canvas_list_account_users(account_id, per_page, page, session_id, search_term) — paginated user directory, 20 users per page.

Do NOT create, update, delete, or submit anything. Read-only. Do not write any files.

ASSIGNED JOB:
For each of these Canvas course IDs: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 — do all of the following: (a) call canvas_get_course_grades with type=["TeacherEnrollment"] and per_page=100, and record every returned enrollment's user_id (note pagination.total_count too); (b) call canvas_get_course_grades with type=["TaEnrollment"] and per_page=100, and record any returned user_ids; (c) call canvas_get_course_grades with type=["StudentEnrollment"] and per_page=1, and record pagination.total_count as the course's student count; (d) call canvas_list_assignments and count how many assignment objects are returned. Output ONLY a compact JSON array, one object per course: {"course_id":N,"teacher_user_ids":[...],"ta_user_ids":[...],"students":N,"assignment_count":N}. Do not include assignment details.

When done, output ONLY a compact JSON code block with the exact structure requested in your job. Keep it minimal — no assignment details, no student records, no extra commentary.

Create an Excel workbook. This is a well-scoped local artifact task.

## Data source (read it first)
Read this JSON file — it contains the complete, final, pre-computed dataset you must transcribe EXACTLY (do not recompute or alter any number, do not re-sort, do not drop or add rows):
`/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-canvas-faculty-workload-review/workspace/workload_data.json`

It contains keys: `standards`, `instructor_load_columns`, `instructor_load` (33 rows), `department_summary_columns`, `department_summary` (7 rows), `totals`.
The rows are ALREADY sorted correctly (instructor_load alphabetically by Instructor; department_summary alphabetically by Department). Keep that order.

## Deliverable
Create the file:
`/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-canvas-faculty-workload-review/workspace/Faculty_Workload.xlsx`

It must contain exactly two worksheets:

**Sheet 1 — named exactly `Instructor Load`**
Header row (row 1) with exactly these 7 column names, in this order:
`Instructor`, `Courses_Count`, `Total_Students`, `Total_Assignments`, `Est_Grading_Hours`, `Weekly_Grading_Hours`, `Overloaded_YN`
Then the 33 data rows from `instructor_load`, in the given order.
- `Est_Grading_Hours` and `Weekly_Grading_Hours` must be written as NUMBERS rounded to 1 decimal place (e.g. 145.2, 11.4) — not strings, not full floats.
- `Courses_Count`, `Total_Students`, `Total_Assignments` as integers.
- `Overloaded_YN` is the text `Y` or `N`.

**Sheet 2 — named exactly `Department Summary`**
Header row (row 1) with exactly these 4 column names, in this order:
`Department`, `Instructor_Count`, `Course_Count`, `Total_Students`
Then the 7 data rows from `department_summary`, in the given order. All counts as integers.

## Formatting requirements (light but professional)
- Make header rows bold with a filled background.
- Auto-size / widen columns so no value is truncated.
- Do not add any extra columns, extra sheets, totals rows, or blank separator rows. The workbook must contain ONLY the data described above, starting at cell A1 on each sheet.

Use the `mcp__excel__*` tools (e.g. `mcp__excel__create_workbook`, `mcp__excel__write_data_to_excel`, `mcp__excel__format_range`, `mcp__excel__rename_worksheet`). The workbook's default sheet may be renamed to `Instructor Load`.

## Report back
When done, verify your work by reading the file back (`mcp__excel__read_data_from_excel` / `get_workbook_metadata`) and report: the absolute file path, the sheet names, the header row of each sheet, the number of data rows on each sheet, and the first and last data row of each sheet. Do NOT paste the entire contents back.
Build Faculty_Workload.xlsx

Create a PowerPoint presentation. This is a well-scoped local artifact task.

## Data source (read it first)
Read this JSON file — it contains the complete, final, pre-computed faculty workload dataset. Use its numbers EXACTLY as given; do not recompute anything:
`/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-canvas-faculty-workload-review/workspace/workload_data.json`

Keys: `standards`, `instructor_load_columns`, `instructor_load` (33 rows), `department_summary_columns`, `department_summary` (7 rows), `totals`.

Key figures already computed for you:
- 33 instructors with a teaching role; 23 are overloaded (Y) and 10 are not (N).
- 22 course offerings; 32,593 total students; 7 departments.
- No instructor teaches more than 3 courses, so ALL 23 overloads are caused by weekly grading hours exceeding the 40-hour limit — not by course count (limit is 4).
- Every one of the 22 offerings exceeds the 200-student recommended maximum per course.
- The one unstaffed offering is "Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2014)" (1,613 students) — no instructor is assigned to it.
- Highest-load instructors (weekly grading hours): Dr. George Allen 145.2, Dr. Caleb Morgan 116.8, Dr. Connor Harris 101.2, Dr. Andrew Walker 85.2, Dr. David Scott 81.9.
- Economics is the ONLY department with zero overloaded instructors.

## Deliverable
Create the file:
`/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-canvas-faculty-workload-review/workspace/Workload_Review.pptx`

It must contain exactly 4 slides:

**Slide 1 — Title slide**
Title: "Faculty Workload Review"
Subtitle: "Faculty Workload Balance Analysis Across All Departments"

**Slide 2 — "Overall Workload Snapshot"**
State the total number of instructors and how many are overloaded. Include the supporting figures: 33 instructors with a teaching role, 23 overloaded (70%), 10 within limits, 22 course offerings, 32,593 total students, 7 departments. A small KPI table or clean bullet layout works well. Mention the policy thresholds (max 4 courses per semester; max 40 weekly grading hours; 0.5 grading hours per student over 16 weeks).

**Slide 3 — "Department-Level Breakdown"**
A table with columns Department, Instructor_Count, Course_Count, Total_Students populated from `department_summary` (7 rows: Analytics 3/2/748, Biochemistry 8/4/7909, Computing 3/2/4434, Design 8/4/6272, Economics 4/3/2934, Finance 8/4/7762, Governance 6/3/2534). You may add a chart if it fits cleanly, but the table is required.

**Slide 4 — "Recommendations: Rebalancing Strategies"**
Concrete bullets targeting the departments with overloaded faculty. Cover at least these points, phrased in your own professional wording:
1. Biochemistry, Finance and Design carry the heaviest student loads — in Biochemistry and Finance every one of their instructors is overloaded; prioritise hiring or cross-departmental reassignment there first.
2. Redistribute the unstaffed "Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2014)" offering (1,613 students) to a currently non-overloaded instructor rather than adding it to an overloaded one.
3. Use Economics as the first source of spare capacity — it is the only department with zero overloaded faculty and holds weekly grading capacity headroom.
4. Since no instructor exceeds the 4-course cap, rebalancing must reduce STUDENT LOAD, not course count — split or co-teach the largest offerings (Creative Computing & Culture Fall 2014 with 2,498 students; Foundations of Finance Fall 2014 with 2,365; Biochemistry & Bioinformatics Fall 2014 with 2,292).
5. Every offering exceeds the recommended 200-student maximum — introduce section caps and additional teaching assistants for grading support.
6. Align assignment counts toward the recommended 10 per course and use staged/rubric-based assessment to cut grading hours.

## Style
Use the `mcp__pptx__*` tools. Professional, clean business style; consistent color scheme; readable font sizes (nothing below ~12pt in the table); no text overflowing off the slides. Save the file to the exact path above.

## Report back
Verify by extracting the text back (`mcp__pptx__extract_presentation_text`) and report: the absolute file path, number of slides, and a one-line confirmation that all four required slides and their key figures are present. Do NOT dump the entire deck back.
